newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium hits fresh highs on options deal.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium hits fresh highs on options deal.

text.p: LME aluminium marched to a fresh 19-month peak on Friday morning on options-related and fund buying, dealers said.
"There was a big options deal done in fourth quarter 1997 and first-half 1998 call options," one dealer said.
The hedging on those options, together with follow-through buying from funds and the Far East pushed prices to a high of $1,723 per tonne.
This is up $22 from Thursday's afternoon kerb close and the highest since December 15, 1995. An options dealer said aluminium business was hectic on Friday morning.
LME data showed a turnover of 9,899 lots in aluminium options for Thursday, with the bulk in calls, 7,649 lots. A breakdown of months and strikes was not immediately available.
Open interest at the $1,700 strike and above in nearby months was already substantial and analysts had warned of a squeeze involving uncovered option grantors.
The LME options declaration for August is next Wednesday.
Spreads have flared this week and on Friday morning the cash/threes dipped into a $2/$5 backwardation.
By 0915 GMT, three months was indicated at $1,714/17, but speculators were expected to gun for upside stops in the rings.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see them go for stops around $1,725," a dealer said, referring to the December 1995 peak.
The other metals also gravitated to the upside.
Zinc hit a $1,495 high in early trading, but eased back to be last indicated at $1,455/60, virtually unchanged from Thursday's kerb close.
Funds were still taking advantage of highs to liquidate remaining long positions, dealers said.
And as long as the market failed to stay above its 30-day moving average at $1,484 it was vulnerable to more technical selling, chartists said.
A stocks rise of 5,100 tonnes also put a damper on the upside but consumers were underpinning the downside for the time being, analysts said.
The cash/threes backwardation was remaining stubbornly wide, indicated at $80/$90, out $5 from Thursday evening.
Copper surged to a high of $2,338, but came off to be last indicated at $2,313/17, versus Thursday's close of $2,318.
A stocks increase of 7,150 tonnes put a dent in sentiment after a lower than usual 850 tonnes increase on Thursday.
"Prices are likely to find it difficult making headway on the upside given rising stocks on both sides of the Atlantic and amid the contracting backwardation," broker Brandeis said.
The back was indicated slightly narrower at $30/$35.
Nickel was unchanged at $7,430 ahead of an announcement by Canada's Falconbridge due at 1200 GMT on the result of labour talks. A contract expires on Friday.
Lead was quiet but marked higher to $639/42 from Thursday's $632 after holding above recent $625 lows.
Tin gained $25 to $5,570 and further gains may be seen with resistance pegged at $5,690.
Alloy last traded at $1,522 compared to $1,515/25.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
